name: Buran OK-GLI (BTS-002)
best_known_for: Buran's atmospheric analog — equivalent of NASA's Enterprise. Four jet engines, 24 atmospheric test flights 1985-1988 at the Zhukovsky LII airfield. Never reached space
credit: Officially BTS-002 (Bolshoy Tranzportnyy Samolyot — Large Transport Aircraft), nicknamed OK-GLI. Full-scale atmospheric test article for the Buran orbital programme — same outer mold-line as the flight vehicle Buran 1.01 but fitted with four AL-31 turbojet engines so it could take off under its own power from a conventional runway. 24 atmospheric flights between 1985-11-10 and 1988-04-15 at the Zhukovsky Flight Research Institute (LII) airfield validated Buran's automated landing system + flight-control software for the 1988-11-15 orbital flight. Notable flights from the 24-flight programme: maiden runway taxi + lift-off 1985-11-10 (Igor Volk, Rimantas Stankyavichus); first fully-automated landing 1987-03-27 (validating the autoland system used on the 1988-11-15 orbital Buran flight); final test flight 1988-04-15 sealing the atmospheric campaign before the orbital flight. After the Buran programme cancellation OK-GLI sat at LII for years; sold to an Australian museum in 1999, then to Bahrain, finally acquired by the Technik Museum Speyer / Sinsheim in Germany where it is on display today — the Buran equivalent of NASA's Enterprise on display at the Intrepid Museum, NYC.
